entities.name: PMID:27495386
observations: Retrospective validation study of 1,188 Mexican adults undergoing cardiac valve surgery at Instituto Nacional de Cardiología Ignacio Chávez, 2004-2008.
Observed mortality was 9.68% versus 5.0% predicted by additive EuroSCORE and 5.6% by logistic EuroSCORE.
Hosmer-Lemeshow calibration was poor for both models (P<0.001); authors concluded EuroSCORE underestimated mortality, especially in intermediate- and high-risk patients.
Additive EuroSCORE risk strata: observed versus predicted mortality was 0.7% versus 2.0% in low risk, 6.34% versus 3.9% in intermediate risk, and 17.4% versus 7.64% in high risk.
Discrimination was modest: AUC 0.707 additive and 0.694 logistic EuroSCORE.

entities.name: Mexican valve surgery
observations: In the identified Mexican valve-surgery cohort, overall observed mortality exceeded both additive and logistic EuroSCORE predictions; underprediction was concentrated in intermediate- and high-risk groups.
No additional mixed-cardiac-surgery Mexican validation cohort with extractable observed-versus-predicted mortality was identified in the search.
Observed-to-expected mortality ratios were approximately 1.94 for additive EuroSCORE and 1.73 for logistic EuroSCORE.
